description: Inserts a new runs row with status 'pending' and returns the generated run_id.
signature: def create_run(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, config: dict, parameters_version: str, trigger_type: str = 'manual', parent_run_id: str | None = None, code_version: str | None = None, notes: str | None = None) -> str
docstring:
Create a new run.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    config: JSON-serializable dict of orchestration.PipelineConfig.to_dict() -- the run-specific choices that are NOT FORMULATION.md-governed (start_stage, max_catalog_pages, request_budget_override, notes). Does not duplicate AcquisitionConfig/EnrichmentParams/AnalysisParams: those are reconstructable from parameters_version plus the git-tracked config/parameters.toml at that version. This is also why create_run can run before config.load_parameters -- config here needs no parsed parameter dataclass to exist yet, only a PipelineConfig, which never depends on FORMULATION.md.
    parameters_version: Output of config.parameters_version(...), a content hash computed directly from the parameters.toml file bytes -- deliberately cheap enough to not require load_parameters to have succeeded, so create_run can be the very first preflight step even ahead of parameter validation.
    trigger_type: 'manual' or 'scheduled'. Only 'manual' is used in v1; 'scheduled' is reserved (ARCHITECTURE.md forward-compatibility note).
    parent_run_id: Reserved for future incremental re-crawls; None in v1.
    code_version: Optional identifier (e.g. a short git hash) of the running code.
    notes: Optional free user text, stored verbatim in the runs.notes column.

Returns:
    The generated run_id: a UTC-timestamp-prefixed, lexicographically sortable, human-readable string (e.g. '20260920T143012Z-a1b2c3'), guaranteed unique within this database.

Raises:
    StorageError: If config is not JSON-serializable, or trigger_type is not one of the two allowed values, or parent_run_id references a run_id that does not exist in runs.
preconditions: parent_run_id is None or already present in runs
postconditions: Two calls to create_run in the same process never return the same run_id, even within the same second, due to the random suffix
run_id values are lexicographically sortable by creation time

edge_cases.input: config containing a non-JSON-serializable value (e.g. a Path object left un-stringified)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError naming the offending key, raised before any row is written
StorageError (would otherwise violate the foreign key silently succeed if foreign_keys were off; foreign_keys=ON per ADR-001 makes sqlite3 raise IntegrityError, wrapped as StorageError)

edge_cases.input: Two create_run calls issued within the same microsecond from two threads on two separate connections
edge_cases.expected_behavior: both succeed with distinct run_ids (random suffix collision probability treated as negligible; a retry-on-collision loop is used defensively)

unit_tests.name: test_create_run_returns_sortable_ids
unit_tests.description: Two sequential calls produce run_ids where the second sorts after the first.

unit_tests.name: test_create_run_roundtrips_through_get_run
unit_tests.description: All fields passed to create_run are readable back unchanged via get_run.
unit_tests.expected: RunRecord with matching config, parameters_version, status='pending'
